subject: Backup deletion propagation and visibility SLA for Acme Health
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Backup retention / deletion propagation question

Hi Markus / Marissa,

We're doing a security review for Acme Health ahead of go-live and need to confirm how Redwood handles deletion requests that originate from the application layer. Two concrete questions:

1) When we delete a patient record (or a whole account) via the API, how long until that deletion is reflected in backups / DR replicas?  Is there any guaranteed SLA for backup purge propagation?
2) Do you provide cryptographic attestation or an audit log proving that backups containing the deleted data were purged? We need something we can attach to our audit artifacts for HIPAA.

Notes/context: Acme uses cross-region replication (us-west, us-east) and we push snapshots to a cold tier (managed offsite snapshots) every 24h. Please include both the standard/default behaviour and whether there's an expedited/paid option to accelerate erasure.

Thanks — appreciate concise concrete numbers so we can feed them to compliance.

— Morgan
Morgan Lee
Security & Privacy, Acme Health

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Backup retention / deletion propagation question

Morgan — thanks for the clear questions. Quick reply with a high-level summary and follow-up items below.

High-level (short):
- Hot-tier caches: deletion tombstoned and cache entries removed within minutes.
- Primary store: data is logically deleted immediately; physical purge depends on backup retention windows and GC.
- Standard backup retention: 90 days by default for snapshots; cold/offsite snapshots follow retention policy — full physical removal can take longer (see below).
- Expedited erase: we offer an "emergency purge" process that can accelerate cross-region GC (requires paperwork and has a discrete fee). Typical expedited window: 7	6 days.

Details I need from you to give firm SLA numbers: account_id or sample object id, and whether any legal holds are in place.

I'll loop in our DR/infra engineer (Connor) and attach our internal one-page summary of the deletion process. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk the flow and what evidence we can provide.

Attaching: draft-delete-process-summary.pdf (internal draft; will provide customer-ready verbiage once we agree).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: backup purge propagation notes for Acme request

Quick internal notes / suggested language we can send to Acme. Putting concrete ranges and what we can commit to:

Summary (recommended customer-facing numbers):
- T0: Deletion request accepted by API -> logical tombstone applied immediately (minutes).
- T0 + 0-30 mins: Hot-tier cache and in-memory KV entries evicted.
- T0 + 1-24 hrs: Background sync flags snapshot index entries as "contains tombstoned objects". This means new restores will not include the object.
- T0 + 3-7 days (standard): Local region GC runs remove tombstoned data from rolling block storage for hot and warm tiers. This is the typical time for data to be physically reclaimed in primary region under default retention (assuming no hold).
- T0 + 7-45 days (cold/offsite snapshots): Offsite snapshot lifecycle (tiered archives) means physical deletion from offsite copies can take longer; our safe window for full physical removal under default policy is up to 45 days.

Expedited option (emergency purge):
- Trigger: Formal customer request + signed attestation form + PO/fee or addendum.
- SLA target: 3-21 days depending on replication topology and third-party archive provider lead times.
- Deliverable: Signed removal attestation (PDF) + export of tamper-evident audit logs covering job lifecycle.

Other notes:
- Cross-region replicas: we mark replicas immediately on the control plane; however offsite snapshot ingest/GC is subject to each replica's archive retention and vendor hold times.
- Encryption: all backups are encrypted at rest. If customer holds keys (CMK), we can provide key-rotation info; immediate key destruction is not a substitute for deletion unless agreed in contract.

Attachments referenced: DR-RTO-RPO-matrix.xlsx (internal), suggested attestation template (we should produce).

Suggested next step: send the recommended customer-facing copy (I can draft), and offer a 30-minute call with Acme + our infra/security engineer to finalize.

-Connor

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Backup retention / deletion propagation question

Morgan — following up with the consolidated, customer-facing answers we discussed internally. Below is the short-form you can include in audit materials; happy to join a call to walk through the flow.

Customer-facing summary (what Redwood will state in SOC/attestation):
- Logical deletion: When an API delete call is accepted (account id acme-prod-7781), Redwood applies a logical tombstone immediately. This prevents subsequent restores or live reads from returning the deleted object.
- Hot/warm tiers: Cache and in-memory copies are evicted within minutes. Persistent block storage in the primary region is reclaimed as part of rolling GC; typical physical reclamation window under our default retention is 3	7 days.
- Cold/offsite snapshots: Because snapshots are copied to tiered archive providers, physical removal from all copies may take up to 45 days under default policies.
- Cross-region replication: Deletion is flagged across control plane at T0; each region then follows its own GC and archive retention. We commit to coordinating cross-region purges and notifying you when each region's purge completes.
- Evidence and attestation: Redwood will provide: (a) a signed removal attestation PDF with timestamps, (b) tamper-evident audit logs for the deletion job (exportable), and (c) a listing of snapshot IDs and region status.
- Expedited (emergency purge) option: available with a Customer Erase Addendum and PO. Target SLA: 3	7 days depending on archive vendor lead times and region count. Exact SLA will be included in the Erase Addendum for the customer.

Required steps from Acme to initiate expedited purge:
1) Complete the Acme Delete Request Form (link: https://redwood.app/drive/Acme-Delete-Request-Form).
2) Confirm there are no legal holds.
3) Sign the Customer Erase Addendum (we will provide template) and PO/fee as applicable.

Attached: draft-delete-process-summary.pdf, DR-RTO-RPO-matrix.xlsx.

If you want an explicit attestation sample I can send one next-day. Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call (we can include our infra/security engineer and provide a redlineable Erase Addendum)?

Best,
